title: Why we offer lamps in Kartika
excerpt: The Damodarashtakam, a broken pot of yoghurt, and why a small flame is so precious in this month.
body: Kartika is called the king of months. The Padma Purana describes the offering of a single lamp in this month as pleasing to Lord Damodara beyond all other offerings.
The pastime behind it is simple. Mother Yashoda could not tie her child until He allowed Himself to be tied. His devotees offer lamps remembering the Lord who is conquered only by love.
At the temple every evening the hall dims, the Damodarashtakam begins, and hundreds of small flames move in circles before the altar. You are welcome to come and offer one.

title: How to begin chanting at home
excerpt: A simple first week of japa, starting with a single round.
body: You do not need anything special to begin. Hare Krishna Hare Krishna, Krishna Krishna Hare Hare, Hare Rama Hare Rama, Rama Rama Hare Hare. Say it clearly and listen to the sound.
Start with one round of 108 on beads, at the same time each day. The early morning is best. When it becomes a habit, add a round.
If you don't have beads yet, use the chanting page on this site, or pick up a set at the temple shop after darshan.

title: Janmashtami 2026 at Hare Krishna Dham
excerpt: A midnight abhisheka, the Lord's birthday feast, and thousands of visitors through the night.
body: The temple opened its doors before dawn on 4 September and did not close them until after the midnight abhisheka. Volunteers managed queues, shoe stalls and prasadam counters through the day.
Thank you to every family who sponsored bhoga, flowers and decoration. The next big celebration is the Kartika month. We hope to see you for the lamp offering.
